title: Markdown preview shows an unhandled exception when WebView2 initialization times out (0x800705B4)

confidence.rationale: The supplied stack and current callback catch establish the escaping error path. The reporter draft and disposal/overlap behavior have not been independently compiled or executed, so validation is still required.

proposed_fixes.title: Handle deferred WebView2 initialization failures in Markdown preview
verification: Build the existing Markdown preview test project with the repository build script, then run its focused tests with vstest.
Exercise delayed initialization success, deterministic COM failure, disposal-before-completion and overlapping preview completion; verify failed WebView2 resources are released.
Repeat the reported CPU-load Explorer Markdown scenario, then preview another file and confirm recovery without an unhandled exception dialog.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: DoPreview schedules an async-void completion callback. A COM controller-initialization failure is neither a NullReferenceException nor inside the lifetime of the outer synchronous catch, so it reaches the WinForms unhandled-exception path.
plan: In MarkdownPreviewHandlerControl.cs, continue from the reporter draft: represent both environment and controller initialization as one Task and observe its completion inside the actual callback error boundary.

Reuse the localized MarkdownNotPreviewedError presentation and existing telemetry pattern. Dispose failed browser resources and avoid adding controls or touching a preview that was unloaded, disposed or superseded; do not silently swallow initialization errors.

In UnitTests-MarkdownPreviewHandler/MarkdownPreviewHandlerTest.cs, inject COMException0x800705B4 after initialization starts. Verify an active preview shows the localized error, no Application.ThreadException escapes, and a disposed/superseded preview receives no late controls.
Preserve normal Markdown navigation/resource restrictions and successful preview behavior; do not disable timeout reporting or merely lengthen a timeout.

information_gaps.why_needed: Catching the COM failure is necessary, but an unsafe late callback could still update the wrong or disposed preview.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Maintainer runs deterministic fault-injection/completion-order tests in the existing Markdown preview test project, then the supplied CPU-load reproduction.
information_gaps.information: Whether the proposed boundary safely handles delayed initialization after unload/disposal and overlapping previews while retaining successful navigation

inferences: A local initialization error boundary should prevent the unhandled-dialog symptom, but does not establish or repair the underlying WebView2 timeout cause.
issue_context.analysis: The stack and current source support a missed asynchronous initialization-error boundary. The reason WebView2 times out under load remains unproven, but a recoverable initialization failure should not escape into an unhandled WinForms dialog. Continue from the reporter draft instead of inventing another timeout workaround.
known_information: The reporter reproduces Markdown preview initialization timeouts under CPU load on multiple machines, with PowerToys0.102.2933 and Windows11. The report includes exact steps, a stack and an exception attachment.
The supplied exception attachment confirms COMException0x800705B4 while WebView2 creates its controller, escaping the Markdown DoPreview async callback into the WinForms exception path.

Current main8827f848fbbac4afeedcae2907c71cd05fd5aa86 still registers an async OnCompleted callback that catches only NullReferenceException; DoPreview has an outer synchronous catch that cannot catch a later async-void failure.

The reporter already supplied a two-file draft correction and fault-injection test in the discussion. No matching repair PR was found by issue-number search or timeline; the proposed patch is not a merged or validated fix.
Related18125 concerns SVG preview timeout behavior, not proof that the Markdown error-handling defect is already fixed.

prerequisites: Windows11 with WebView2 runtime and Markdown preview enabled; an ordinary local Markdown file; controlled development/test environment.
steps: 1. Reproduce the supplied Explorer sequence during a controlled CPU-heavy build; record whether the controller timeout becomes an unhandled dialog.
2. In the existing test project, arrange an initialization task that fails asynchronously with COMException0x800705B4 and verify the preview error UI and failed-browser disposal.
3. Complete initialization only after unload/disposal or after a replacement preview starts; ensure no stale controls, wrong-file navigation or unhandled thread exception.
4. Restore normal initialization, preview Markdown successfully, and confirm navigation/resource restrictions remain unchanged.
setup: Enable Explorer preview pane. Use the existing Markdown preview test project for deterministic failed initialization rather than relying solely on CPU stress.
reproduce.title: Verify Markdown handles asynchronous WebView2 controller failure
reproduce.expected_result: Initialization failure produces the existing localized preview error without an unhandled dialog; disposed or superseded previews remain untouched and later previews can succeed.
